procedure.method: Independent fresh critic session; no spawning, forking, resuming, peer review, producer explanation or unlisted embedded path was used. Read the literal packet/case, pinned rubric/rules and compact method/addendum. The packet declares zero source assets and zero protected-layout manifests, so there were no source opens or protected-layout reads to perform. Read all five exact pinned native-evidence manifests before poster viewing, without following their embedded source/input/final paths. Verified the pins, byte counts and PNG-header dimensions of all fifteen declared poster assets. Actually opened and visually inspected each through tools.view_image with detail original, forwarding its returned image_url with image at original detail: M1 native, usage720, thumbnail320; then M2, M3, M4 and M5 in that same three-view order. All fifteen returned images were displayed and inspected before the first poster copy-reading/transcription stage, judgment or score. After the fifteenth display, read the poster text from those already displayed exact views in member/copy order; did not reopen an image or use OCR, required-text substitution or a transcription revisit. Judged only visible pixels. The two 1672x941 landscapes pass 16:9 by the declared single-edge rounding: 941 differs from 1672*9/16=940.5 by 0.5 pixel; they are not mathematically exact 16:9. The three 1024x1536 portraits are mathematically exact 2:3. Usage views are 720x405 or 720x1080; thumbnails are 320x180 or 213x320, with aspect preserved to integer sampling and no upsampling. Actual session identity is unavailable here and remains null.

The slender serif Hangul title has deliberate open spacing; the plainer body retains clear syllable blocks, word spaces, commas and periods.
Cream letters remain clean against the dark glass/pavement and line spacing supports continuous reading without collisions.
left text edges and glass diagonal
Both text blocks share a clear left inset while the lower glass edge creates a diagonal that leads away from the body into the right foreground.
The open interval is occupied by street activity and light rather than an unused information-template gap.
droplets, panel mullions and bottom-right tiles
Sharp pane edges and near wet tile texture coexist coherently with softer traffic and pedestrians at depth. Amber reflections follow the wet surface and window framing.
The depth and reflective surface relationships survive downsampling; bright bokeh remains controlled enough to preserve the street.

window framing, wet floor and traffic silhouettes

Strong directional crops and dry grain produce a tactile, alert street mood; the restrained orange wear accents focus the force instead of scattering many colors. An energetic open-style treatment can serve attentive noticing.

Several image fragments remain visually disconnected: the upper silhouette lacks a cleanly resolved leg/ground boundary, and the orange-edged oval overlays separate stripe systems without an intelligible join. These unresolved local relationships leave an assembled-stock-fragment quality.

residuals: The exact function of the orange-speckled curved object cannot be identified confidently from the pixels; it is recorded as a curved worn detail, without inventing a puddle, handrail, wheel or maker story.

The upper dark fragments suggest shoes/walking but their precise leg/shadow/ground boundaries remain weak. This visible lack of scene legibility drives content_form3, image_material3 and ai_slop3; all assets and copy remain assessable.

evidence: whole landscape and reflective right half

Full-bleed wet-street photography, amber against blue-black, thin light serif title and small light sans body produce a quiet cinematic identity. Continuous glass/reflection depth distinguishes it from the other four constructed graphic or painted images, including the blue daylight of M4.

Three angular orange trouser-and-shoe units, smooth undulating blue bands, floating yellow quadrilaterals and large blue loops make a bright schematic graphic. Its bold gothic voice and navy/cream family overlap M5, but its clean planar repeated figures and horizontal rhythm differ substantially from M5's coarse cropped montage.
diagonal alley, upper-left title and orange window

Black silhouette architecture cuts a continuous rising alley into ivory; a receding paired trail and one orange domestic window are joined by dense heavy serif lettering. It shares a two-line title and alley subject with M4, but flat cut edges, near-binary contrast and nocturnal enclosure give it a separate whole identity.

Blue sky, warm plaster, cool roof shadows, visible painterly strokes and softer dark serif copy make an airy upward-looking scene. Its continuous daylight atmosphere and expansive sky differ from M3's compressed black alley and from M1's wet nocturnal glass.
diagonal crops around the central ivory text island

Coarse navy halftone, orange-speckled curved detail, cropped dark shoe-like silhouettes and several directional stripe fields surround a very heavy gothic title. The rough close-up fragments and irregular text island differ from M2's smooth complete vector units and M3's coherent long-view silhouette scene.
relationships across all five finished members

The set varies image framing/editing, contrast structure, finish, type voice and emotional effect together. M1 is reflective and cinematic, M2 schematic and buoyant, M3 enclosed and graphic, M4 airy and painterly, and M5 forceful and tactile. These are observed composite differences rather than five material names or palette/filter changes. All five are independent opaque single-poster compositions.
residuals: Diversity is resolved at 4, not exceptional: the navy/cream heavy-gothic pairing of M2/M5 and the serif two-line alley pairing of M3/M4 remain family resemblances. Shared reading order is allowed and was not treated as a mandatory defect.

Count and diversity do not erase M2's literal content shortfall or the low dimension records for M2 and M5. This record supplies one independent critic; it does not establish the other two critics' judgments or a combined all-three gate.
